Connecting at E6 ties E5-F6 together solidly and keeps pressure on White's D5 group, setting up D4 as a strong follow-up.

If I play D4 first instead, White's E6 becomes atari-threatening against F6, and my F5 connect ends up doing little while White builds a solid E6-E7-F7 wall. Still, I lean toward prioritizing D4 since securing the bottom territory matters more; I'm trying to count whether Black can reach roughly 45 points this way, tallying up the rows plus E5, F5, G5, F6 and the J4/J5 area.

Running the numbers more carefully, White's right-side group plus the top looks too strong -- their total comes to around 41 against my 40, which isn't enough.
